game: GB @ CLE Week 3 2025, kickoff 2025-09-21 13:00 ET, outdoor Cleveland, CLE +8.5, total 41.5

script.base: Books have Green Bay leading a moderate outdoor game: GB implied 25.0, Cleveland 16.5. Base flow is GB ahead by halftime, closing with Josh Jacobs (42 carries, 150 yards in weeks 1-2) while Cleveland, already negative EPA per dropback (-0.56 vs blitz, -0.15 vs none), trails and throws. Pace is not a shootout; both run defenses have allowed one 10-plus run in two games.
script.flip1: GB gets up big early, runs the clock, Love's attempts and WR yards stall, Jacobs' carry count spikes, and Cleveland only accumulates through garbage-time throws.
script.flip2: Cleveland hangs around if Bitonio and Conklin play, the game stays within a score, GB has to throw, Jacobs' rush volume dips, and the Sampson/Ford/Judkins split stays alive.

injury_fallout: Pre-kick nflverse report only; final inactives not in the pack. GB WR Jayden Reed is Out (foot): 5 targets, 45 yards, 70 air yards come off the board. Next shares on file are Kraft 11 targets/140 yards (Questionable, knee), Doubs 9/96/177 air, Wicks 8/74/151 air, Brooks 5/29, Golden 4/16/91 air, Musgrave 3/36. CLE DT Mike Hall Jr. Out (knee) dents an otherwise elite run front (2.32 YPC, 1 run of 10+). CLE G Joel Bitonio Questionable (back) and T Jack Conklin Questionable (elbow): if either sits, Cleveland rush efficiency and pass protection get worse. Judkins (10 carries, 61 yards) is not on the report, so the committee is assumed active.

Reed's vacated air yards sit with Doubs (177 air) and Wicks (151 air) against a defense that has allowed explosives. Cleveland's primary Jeudy (16 targets, 202 air, 117 yards) runs into GB's suppressed outside YPA; Fannin (14 targets, 92 air, 111 yards) is the better fit for GB's relative middle softness, capped by a 16.5 team total.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Cleveland stayed competitive, so the abandon-run script never showed and Sampson got a 29-yard type day against a GB run defense that had only two games of 2.45 YPC on the sheet. Separately, GB led early, Love handed it to Jacobs, the questionable tackle pushed Green Bay into quick game, and Reed's targets went to Doubs and Kraft while Wicks, who had turned 151 air yards into only 74 receiving yards, finished in the 20s. The counter-case is strong enough that neither leg is more than a lean, and a single competitive-game flip beats Sampson while a blowout flip beats Wicks.
slip_story: Base-script card only, not a shootout and not a total-under mixed with same-game overs. Story: GB leads, Cleveland chases and stops feeding the committee, Sampson rush under 17.5 hits; Reed's absence gives Wicks a path to a low 37.5 inside a 25-point GB total. They share the base script and fail on different flips (Sampson dies if it stays close; Wicks dies if GB runs the clock early), so do not treat them as a locked pair. Tighter correlation if the human wants one story with one failure mode: swap Wicks for Ford rushyds under 19.5. No TDs. Kraft stays off the slip while questionable.
